privacy.metaDescription: What {{appName}} does with personal data: account, household, expenses, and your rights.
privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This notice explains what {{appName}} does with personal data. It follows the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) and the French Data Protection Act (Loi n° 78-17 du 6 janvier 1978, as amended).
privacy.controllerBody: {{appName}} is published by its operator, who is the controller. No data protection officer is appointed: Article 37 of the GDPR does not require one for this service. To exercise your rights or ask a question, write to {{email}}.
privacy.controllerBodyNoEmail: {{appName}} is published by its operator, who is the controller. No data protection officer is appointed: Article 37 of the GDPR does not require one for this service. A public contact email is not set in this deployment. You can still access, correct, export and delete your data from inside the app, as described below.
privacy.dataBody:
Account: email address, a password stored only as a bcrypt hash (or none, if you use Google), an optional Google account identifier, and the date the account was created. A guest does not have a real address: a technical address is stored for that session. One account can belong to several households, as admin, member or guest.

Household: name, type (solo or shared) and how often you review balances.

Members: display name, colour, status (active or archived) and an email. If you do not enter an email, the app stores a technical placeholder that is not a real mailbox.

Money records you enter: expenses, splits, categories, recurring bills, income, settlements and optional notes.

Session: a signed token kept in this browser (local storage), containing only your account id. It expires after 7 days. It is not a cookie.

Language: the language you pick, kept in this browser.

We do not ask for special-category data (health, religion, biometrics and similar). A Google display name is used only once, to suggest a household name, and is not stored as a separate profile field.
privacy.purposesBody:
Running the service you ask for — account, household, expenses, balances and settlements. Legal basis: performance of a contract (Article 6(1)(b) GDPR).

Keeping the account secure and limiting a household to its admin, its members and its guests. Legal basis: contract, and legitimate interest in preventing unauthorised access (Article 6(1)(f)).

Google sign-in, only if you choose it. We then receive your email, whether Google has verified it, and a Google identifier. Legal basis: contract, including the steps you take before creating an account.

Audience measurement of pages visited, without cookies and without your household id (it is removed before the event is sent). Legal basis: legitimate interest in understanding which pages are used (Article 6(1)(f)). This is not advertising and it is not used to profile you.

You can object to processing based on legitimate interest by writing to the contact address. We do not make automated decisions that produce legal effects about you.
privacy.recipientsBody:
The publisher of {{appName}}.

Vercel, Inc. (United States) hosts the website, the API and cookieless audience measurement. Vercel is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.

Neon hosts the database. Household data is stored in the European Union, in Frankfurt (Germany). Neon acts as a processor.

Google LLC, only after you choose Google sign-in. The Google script is not loaded on the home page, and it is not loaded until you click “Continue with Google”.

We do not sell personal data and we do not share it with advertisers.
privacy.transfersBody:
The database is stored in the European Union (Frankfurt, Germany).

The website and the API run on Vercel, a company established in the United States. Vercel is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, an adequacy decision of the European Commission for certified organisations.

Neon is established in the United States. Storage stays in Frankfurt. Neon states that it relies on the Data Privacy Framework for international transfers and offers a data processing agreement.

If you use Google sign-in, Google may process that sign-in outside the European Union under its own terms and the same kind of safeguard.

Fonts are served by this site. Your browser does not contact Google to load them.
privacy.retentionBody:
Account and household data are kept for as long as the account exists.

Deleting a household in Settings erases that household and the data attached to it: members, expenses, income, settlements and the rest. The account stays open. The deletion is immediate in the application database. The database host may keep a backup copy for its own backup window, then delete it.

The session token expires 7 days after it is issued. Signing out removes it from this browser.

Audience measurement does not include a household id or query parameters.
privacy.rightsBody:
Under the GDPR and the French Data Protection Act, you can:

Access your data in the app (account, household, members, expenses, income, balances).

Correct it in the app (household settings, members, expenses).

Delete it: Settings, then delete the household. That erases the data for that household. The account stays open. To delete the account itself, write to the contact address.

Export expenses as CSV from the expenses page. For a copy of the rest, write to the contact address.

Ask us to restrict processing, or object to processing based on legitimate interest, via the contact address.

Lodge a complaint with the CNIL, the French supervisory authority: 3 Place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, France.
privacy.cookiesBody:
This site does not use advertising cookies, and it does not show a cookie banner.

The session and the language preference are stored in the browser’s local storage. They are required to keep you signed in and to remember the language you chose. They are not third-party cookies.

Audience measurement (Vercel Web Analytics) does not use cookies. Before an event is sent, the household id is replaced and query parameters are removed.

Google may set its own cookies only after you click “Continue with Google” on the sign-in or registration page.
privacy.securityBody:
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt before they are stored. They are never kept in clear text and they are never returned by the API.

Each request is checked with a signed token. An account can only open the households it belongs to.

In production the site is served over HTTPS.
privacy.childrenBody: The service is meant for adults who manage a household. In France, the digital age of consent is 15. We do not knowingly create accounts for children under 15. If you believe we have, write to the contact address and the account will be deleted.
privacy.changesBody: This notice may be updated when the service changes. The date at the top of the page is the date of the current version.
privacy.noticeBody:
Publisher: the operator of {{appName}}. Contact: the address given in the first section of this page.

Hosting of the site and the API: Vercel, Inc., United States (https://vercel.com).

Database: Neon, with storage in the European Union (Frankfurt, Germany).

This page is the privacy notice required by Articles 13 and 14 of the GDPR and by the French Data Protection Act. It also names the host, as required for a public website under the French LCEN.

terms.metaDescription: The terms of the service: account, households, invitations, and what the app does not do.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro:
These terms describe the {{appName}} service. Creating an account, or joining a household you were invited to, means you accept them.

The publisher is the operator of {{appName}}. Contact: {{email}}.
terms.serviceBody: {{appName}} keeps a household's expenses, splits, income, balances and settlements in one place. It is a record you keep. It is not a bank, it does not move money, and it does not provide payment services.
terms.accountBody:
You can register with an email address and a password, or with Google if you choose it. One account per email address. The same account can belong to several households, as admin, member or guest.

You are responsible for your password, and for what is entered from your account.
terms.householdBody:
Whoever creates a household is its admin. Other people join only by invitation: as a guest, or with their own account as a member.

An admin manages that household. A member or a guest sees the household they were invited to, within the role they were given. An account cannot open a household it does not belong to.
terms.dataBody: Expenses, income and notes are data you enter. We do not sell personal data and we do not share it with advertisers. The privacy notice explains what is stored, for how long, and the rights you have.
terms.deletionBody:
Deleting a household in Settings erases that household and the data attached to it: members, expenses, income and settlements. The account stays open.

To delete the account itself, write to the contact address.
terms.useBody: Use the service to keep a household record. Do not invite people who did not ask to join, do not try to open a household you do not belong to, and do not try to disrupt the service.
terms.availabilityBody: The service can change, pause or stop. We do not promise that it will be available at every moment. A balance shown in the app is a record of what was entered. It is not, by itself, a court judgment. You decide what to pay, outside the app.
terms.ageBody: The service is meant for adults who manage a household. In France, the digital age of consent is 15. We do not knowingly create accounts for children under 15.
terms.changesBody: These terms may be updated when the service changes. The date at the top of the page is the date of the current version.
terms.lawBody: These terms are governed by French law. If a disagreement remains after you write to the contact address, the French courts have jurisdiction.

help.metaDescription: Short answers about households, invitations and your data.
help.title: FAQ
help.intro: Short answers about households, invitations and your data.
help.whoBody: Whoever creates it is the admin. Other people see it only after an invitation, as a guest or as a member with their own account. Someone without an invitation cannot open it.
help.inviteBody: Add names first, then share a link. Each person picks their name. A guest picks again each visit. An account keeps that name in this household only.
help.deleteBody: In Settings, delete the household. That erases the household and what is attached to it: members, expenses, income and settlements. The account stays open. To delete the account, write to {{email}}.
help.googleTitle: Do I have to use Google?
help.googleBody: No. You can register with an email and a password. The Google script is loaded only after you click “Continue with Google” on the sign-in or registration page.
help.adsBody: No. {{appName}} does not show ads, and your data is not sold.

accessibility.metaDescription: How {{appName}} is built, and how to write if something blocks you.
accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: {{appName}} is a private service. The French accessibility rules for public-sector websites (RGAA) do not apply here. This page is not a conformity declaration, and no accessibility audit has been carried out.
accessibility.effortBody: Amounts are written as numbers, forms have labels, and you can switch the interface between English and French. Colour can signal a positive or negative balance. The amount and the wording still say what the figure means.
accessibility.contactBody: Write to {{email}}. Name the page and what you could not do. We will answer, and correct what we can.

couple.metaDescription: One household for two. Rent, groceries, and who owes what.
couple.title: For a couple
couple.intro: One household for two people. Rent, groceries and the rest, with a clear view of who paid and who owes what.
couple.point1Body: Create the household and invite the other person, with their own account as a member, or as a guest.
couple.point2Body: Equal splits, or a percentage when one of you covers more of a bill. An expense can also stay with one person.
couple.point3Body: Balances show who should pay whom. Record the payment when it is done.

roommates.metaDescription: Roommates: rent and shared bills, with a balance for each person.
roommates.title: For roommates
roommates.intro: Several people, one home. Rent and the shared bills stay in one place, with a balance for each person.
roommates.point1Body: Add each roommate. They join by invitation, as a guest or with their own account.
roommates.point2Body: Split equally, or by percentage when rooms or shares are not the same.
roommates.point3Body: Rent, internet and electricity can repeat each period, already split.

solo.metaDescription: A household just for you. Expenses, income, and what is left to spend.
solo.title: For one person
solo.intro: A household can be just you. Keep expenses, income and what is left to spend, without inviting anyone.
solo.point1Body: Name it and keep it to yourself. You can open another one later, for a home you share.
solo.point2Body: Categories, the recent trend, income and what is left after the bills.
solo.point3Body: Rent, utilities and subscriptions, ready each period, even when nobody else shares them.

bills.metaDescription: Rent, internet, electricity. Bills that return, already split.
bills.title: Shared bills
bills.intro: Rent, internet, electricity. The bills that return every month, split across the people who share them.
bills.point1Body: A recurring expense is ready each period. You do not retype the rent every month.
bills.point2Body: Equal parts, or percentages. You see each person's share before you save.
bills.point3Body: Balances and suggested repayments show who should pay whom, after the bills of the period.
